learnerStatement: Simulated learner. This review finds problems; it is not evidence that anyone learned.
learnerBoundary: Everyday numeracy, simple charts, comparing numbers and familiar household objects; no domain-specific theory assumed.

observations.prediction: Selected 15 km for horizon at 1.7 m beach eye height and locked it in. Initial locked stage instead had 30 m eye height.
observations.exploration: You preset gave 1.7 m to 4.7 km. 100x preset gave 170 m to 47 km. Tower gave 828 m to 103 km. Seen line retained all three pairs and reveal unlocked after tower.
observations.reveal: Corrected 4.7 km. Links grazing sightline/right angle to Pythagoras and square root of twice Earth radius times height. Explains hundredfold height gives tenfold distance. Air refraction makes real horizons farther.
observations.visual: Inline initial and tower screenshots inspected: white tangent sightline to blue curved sea, marked right angle at horizon, 50 km scale. Caption states distances true, curve/height stretched 47x, no refraction. All Seen pairs legible. Trust count 4/4 ignored.
observations.isolation: No-history evaluation preview banner present. Visible trust count ignored.
observations.reference: Own CUA tab 543884122 snapshots and inspected inline screenshot; no screenshot file saved.

prediction.reason: Concrete beach-distance estimate with plausible numeric alternatives.

interaction.reason: Three controlled heights expose slow distance growth and retain comparisons.

payoff.reason: Resolves estimate using retained results, visible geometry and real-world refraction limit.
payoff.evidence: Seen pairs, tangent right angle, hundredfold/tenfold and refraction reveal.

clarity.reason: Presets, history line and explicit distortion caption make core path clear despite different initial height.
clarity.evidence: Inspected tower screenshot and three preset path.

transfer.reason: Reusable square-root rule offered but no concrete new application after rule.
transfer.evidence: Square root of twice radius times height.

accessibility.evidence: Keyboard, focus, contrast audit, phone, zoom/reflow and motion unknown.

surprise.reason: Committed 15 km estimate reversed and hundredfold height produces only tenfold reach.

visualExplanation.reason: Tangent and right-angle geometry show horizon mechanism.

playfulness.reason: Named presets and slider support reversible variation.

depth.reason: Tangent geometry, square-root scaling and refraction boundary connected.

complexity.reason: Uses tangent right triangle and square-root scaling with visual support.
complexity.interfaceBurden: Low: three presets and retained Seen line.
complexity.notationRepresentationBurden: moderate: mixed m/km and square root

whyCool: Raising eye height a hundredfold moves the horizon only ten times farther, and the retained Seen line makes that scaling explicit.
caveat: Slider and a fresh application were not tested; graphic deliberately stretches curve and height.
